questions.q: If the length of a stretched string is shortened by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mo>%</mo></math> and the tension is increased by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>44</mn><mo>%</mo></math> then the ratio of the initial and final fundamental frequencies is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math>, the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>'</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>'</mo></math> is
questions.solution:
Recall the formula of fundamental frequency in terms of tension and mass per unit length,

f=12lTμ

it means,

f1f2=12l1T1μf=12l2T2μ=l2l1×T1T2

Put given data,

12=l1-x100l×TT1+44100⇒12=100-x10×112⇒60=100-x⇒x=40

The minimum and maximum frequency of the sound observed by a listener situated in the plane of the circle is (Speed of sound is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>332</mn><mo> </mo><msup><mi>ms</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.solution:
In one case the source is moving away and in one case this is moving towards while the observer is in rest so using Doppler shift in sound,

f=f0vv±vs,

here the angular velocity is given,

ω=5 rev s-1 and the radius of the circle is, 1π m

so the velocity of the source is,

vs=ωr=5×1π=1.59 m s-1

so apparent frequency,

f=f0vv±vs=500332332±1.59=485.4 Hz & 515.5 Hz
